Neither condition is satisfied here: field-service dispatch remains exposed, below target, and not covered by a completed acceptance. The strongest defensible packet is therefore to certify while narrowing the claim: rely on aggregate readiness and monitoring as operational support, acknowledge the unresolved limitation, and present certification as contingent on disclosure rather than as evidence that the weakness is resolved.

That clarification is useful, but it does not cure the core evidentiary gap. The distinction is decisive: a caveat can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveated condition is already satisfied and merely needs to be stated clearly. Here, the unresolved predicate is whether the required explicit limitation disclosure is actually present in the launch certification packet. On the available record, it is not proven. The Actor also concedes there is no approved risk acceptance and no exclusion of the affected use case. Under the stated policy, rollout controls, rollback, and monitoring do not substitute for that missing requirement while exposure remains. So the present certification claim remains inadequately supported from admissible evidence alone.
